name: HDFC Bank Ltd

ledger.quote: So given that, we do expect that over the next 1 year to 2 years, we would be getting down further into the levels that we had previously been there, call it, the 90s or low 90s and so on.
ledger.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
ledger.verdict: Target timeframe of 1 to 2 years from January 2026 has not elapsed.

ledger.quote: We said we will try and be in a range of somewhere between 90% to 96% in the year FY '26, which is what we will be is what we are very confident about.
ledger.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
ledger.verdict: Management did not report FY26 loan-to-deposit ratio on the call, and financial tables omit loan totals.

ledger.quote: And then maybe by FY '27, by the natural growth and even with the growth in the way we are expecting in terms of faster growth rate, I think we should land somewhere around the 85% to 90% for FY '27.
ledger.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
ledger.verdict: Target timeframe of FY27 has not yet elapsed.

ledger.quote: So if we're talking about 12% to 13%, we are talking about a couple of percentage points above that going into the next year.
ledger.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha
ledger.target: Grow a couple of percentage points above system
ledger.verdict: Total AUM grew 15.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, exceeding the 12% to 13% system growth rate.
ledger.evidence: Total AUM grew 15.3% year-on-year, including a 1.9% impact of FCNR (B) leverage, with SME and retail assets leading the charge.

ledger.quote: So between the physical channels, between the digital channels, between the customer acquisitions and across the set of our core retail products, we do see that growing well.
ledger.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha
ledger.verdict: Retail disbursements accelerated past Rs 90,000 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to Rs 76,000 crore in Q1.
ledger.evidence: The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has crossed Rs 90,000 crores during Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year.

ledger.quote: Our focus now, as I may have mentioned in the past and also in our annual report, we are trying to take customer service to a different level
ledger.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
ledger.target: Take customer service to a different level
ledger.verdict: Service delivery turnaround times reduced by 30% and product delivery turnaround times decreased 10% to 15%.
ledger.evidence: The turnaround times on product deliveries have come down anyway between 10% and 15% in a short span of time, while service delivery TATs have come down by 30% during the quarter.

ledger.quote: Fundamentally, the franchise continues to be extremely strong and we will be stepping up the multiple product offerings and one customer view and you will see the changes happening in the quarters to come.
ledger.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
ledger.target: Step up multiple product offerings and one customer view
ledger.verdict: Retail and MSME teams implemented one view across products and channels for same-day resolution.
ledger.evidence: all working from one view across products and across all channels to ensure a same-day, same-time resolution of delivery of products, services, queries, and complaints as well.

ledger.quote: And so, that mix of the asset is also an important contributor on that.
ledger.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
ledger.verdict: Retail asset mix percentage is not provided in reported figures or specified in the call transcript.

ledger.quote: For a start, the endeavor and our vision is to reach to somewhere near the pre-merger levels or just around the time of the merger, which was around 38.
ledger.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
ledger.target: Reach CASA ratio near pre-merger levels of 38-40%
ledger.verdict: Medium to long term target timeframe has not elapsed since July 2026.

ledger.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth.
ledger.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
ledger.target: Profit growth at or above balance sheet growth
ledger.verdict: Longer term target timeframe has not elapsed since July 2026.

open.quote: And therefore, I think going forward, across the next 2 quarters, you will see that change coming through as we also grow the volumes in retail and MSME.
open.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha

read: Management has consistently delivered on operational enhancements, service turnarounds, and retail disbursement acceleration. However, medium-term balance sheet targets like LDR and CASA ratios remain pending or unmeasured in recent reports.
questions: What was the achieved loan-to-deposit ratio for FY26 relative to the 90% to 96% target range?
What is the present retail asset mix percentage toward the stated 60% goal?
bull: Total AUM grew 15.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, outperforming system credit growth.
Q2 FY27 PAT reached Rs 21,537 crore, rising from Rs 20,364 crore in Sep 2025.
Retail disbursements crossed Rs 90,000 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 76,000 crore in Q1.
bear: Management omitted reporting whether the FY26 LDR target of 90% to 96% was achieved.
Retail asset share toward the 60% target remains unquantified in reported figures.
